problem: Old and new focus were joined into one bounding rectangle, repainting unrelated space between distant buttons.
change: Copy up to eight independent rectangles through the private widget bridge, discard containment, fall back to the full client on overflow, damage only focus underlines, and queue the pressed control first. Existing Layers clipping and completed-strip publication are retained.

pin.scope: GEM VDI development: FX 1.26 at D600, private 512 KiB VRAM, inactive at cold boot. Detection only is tested by G0.

peripherals.name: happy-none
peripherals.firmware: built-in high-level model; quiet command only

observer.mode: same binary, EXEC816_LATENCY_TRACE and EXEC816_MASK_TRACE environment gates; replay with both unset

keyboard_input.mode: POKEY matrix scan; PushRawKey/ReleaseRawKey immediate=false; modifier matrix transitions
keyboard_input.initialization: KEY ALL up enables scan mode before modifier changes

mouse_input.mapping: unmodified built-in preset; all other input maps disabled in isolated test profile
mouse_input.host_path: ATInputManager::OnMouseMove(0, dx, dy); OnButtonChanged(0, MouseLMB, state)
mouse_input.sensitivity: default preset: 16 integer host units per electrical transition; no mapping acceleration
mouse_input.capture: headless scheduled relative motion; GUI uses normal host mouse capture
mouse_input.observer: EXEC816_MOUSE_TRACE=1 logs MOUSE_HOST and passive MOUSE_PHASE in base scheduler cycles; unset for replay
mouse_input.controller_timing: Unmodified slow (scanline) scheduler: each phase delay clamps 0x1000000/remaining fixed-point distance to 1..256 scanlines. The passive observer timestamps output on the base CPU scheduler.

comparison_scope: Same five paced idle actions (Toggle, Large, Apply, Small, Cancel), ten physical ST edges per image, matching final button hashes. Completed scanouts with one PAL frame observation quantization. Not the 100-action loaded AW5 matrix.
release_tradeoff: Apply release feedback takes one extra PAL frame (159.08 to 179.29 ms). Observed status visibility is later for Large (319.49 to 379.87 ms), Small (359.66 to 379.87 ms) and Cancel (279.58 to 319.74 ms). Separate repairs can require more presentation turns; status observation follows the button and can overestimate first label visibility.

raw.bridge: Action! writes all eight signed rectangles and count; C verifies each field and stride, writes different values, and Action! verifies the returned array before running the repeated model/state/input probes.

opt.bridge: Action! writes all eight signed rectangles and count; C verifies each field and stride, writes different values, and Action! verifies the returned array before running the repeated model/state/input probes.

packaged_demo.scope: Desktop OF816 autoboot, widget toggle/radio/momentary/cancel/disabled/default, client drag/focus, disk commands, writable WORK media, seven-Task pipeline and EXIT

memory.accounting: Fixed/root/kernel, each public Task, private idle, guards, alignment and unused reserved capacity included.

limitations: Responsiveness targets remain open; this small idle sample is not loaded timing qualification.
Release/status presentation does not uniformly improve; all per-edge timings and the regressions are retained.
Flicker observation begins after the model/application checkpoint and stops at the first exact button match, excluding the pointer footprint. It is not continuous scanout or whole-gesture proof.
Completed-strip publication is not a whole-window or whole-frame atomic swap. Physical hardware is not qualified.
